We are given a large set of lineage relationships: "X is Y's ancestor" or "X is Y's descendant". Essentially, these are directed edges in a family tree: X ancestor of Y means X is an ancestor of Y (X is older/grandparent etc). Descendant means the reverse: X descendant of Y means Y is ancestor of X. So we have a directed graph where edges represent ancestry (A -> B means A is ancestor of B). We can also infer relationships: if A is ancestor of B, then B is descendant of A. Also transitivity holds: if A is ancestor of B and B is ancestor of C, then A is ancestor of C.
